t: This is the Purcell Room, a small concert hall with three hundred and seventy seats, part of the Southbank Centre. It's the smallest of the three venues here, alongside the Royal Festival Hall and the Queen Elizabeth Hall. The room has hosted chamber music, jazz, mime and poetry recitals. It takes its name from Henry Purcell, the seventeenth-century English composer and organist. He wrote more than a hundred songs, the opera Dido and Aeneas, and the music for The Fairy Queen, a version of A Midsummer Night's Dream.
